label: At D2, high when S2 is reached, low for S1; higher after choosing a1.
terms: (phase == D2) * (state == S2) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) ;; (phase != D2) * belief_lo ;; (phase != D2) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase != D2) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S2) * ep_dec
explanation: Raw reset gate r44 beyond timing is driven almost entirely by the D2 step: the reached state shown at D2 sets it (S2 up, S1 strongly down) and the just-made choice adds on top (a1 up, a2 down), additively, so rare a1->S2 is highest and rare a2->S1 lowest. Both are observed at D2 (no future variables). D1/GO residuals are small (~+-0.03), tracking belief_lo (higher when S1 believed good) and previous choice a1; the free fit adds these plus D2 belief and an episode-late term for only a few points of R^2. Hidden good state, future reward and trials since reversal contribute nothing.

issues: Minor: the S1 and S2 terms only act as a pair. Dropping the S1 term cuts test R^2 beyond timing to 0.45, and swapping it for (state==0) also gives 0.45. So S1 works as a D2-specific offset and S2 as the S1-vs-S2 contrast. The fitted weights (S2 +0.11, S1 -0.27, a1 +0.16) predict D2 residuals of a1S1 -0.11, a1S2 +0.27, a2S1 -0.27 and a2S2 +0.11. These match the profile table (-0.113, +0.271, -0.263, +0.109), so this is a real description, not curve fitting.
Using in_action==1 (the observed last-action input at D2) instead of action==1 gives the same 0.8935 test score, so no future variables are involved.

Misses: mean error by phase is 0. What remains is small systematic error at D1/GO, about +-0.05: under-predicted after a1 trials (D1 after a1 S1 u +0.048), over-predicted after a2 trials (GO after a2 S1 u -0.048). This matches the explanation's small belief and previous-choice effects (belief-decile residuals about +-0.03). The worst windows are late-episode GO steps where the actual value drops to about 0.55-0.65 against a prediction of 0.86. These are scattered and small next to the +-0.27 D2 effect.
The label leaves out that the D1/GO effects are small, but it does correctly limit itself to D2, which carries almost all of the variance (this choice x state reference score 0.92).
